recognition: Cartographic classification in Natural Earth: Sovereign country. This classification is not a statement of international recognition.
provenance: Country facts are from the archived CIA World Factbook mirror. Officeholders and economic/military data are reference observations, not a live update.
capital: Gitega (political capital), Bujumbura (commercial capital) · in January 2019, the Burundian parliament voted to make Gitega the political capital of the country while Bujumbura would remain its economic capital; as of 2023, the government's move to Gitega remains incomplete
rulers: President Evariste NDAYISHIMIYE (since 18 June 2020); Prime Minister Nestor NTAHONTUYE (since 5 August 2025)
economy: highly agrarian, low-income Sub-Saharan economy; declining foreign assistance; increasing fiscal insolvencies; dense and still growing population; COVID-19 weakened economic recovery and flipped two years of deflation GDP (PPP): $11.739 billion (2024 est.). note: data in 2021 dollars
military: Burundi National Defense Force (BNDF; Force de Defense Nationale du Burundi, FDNB): Land Force (Army), Naval Force, Air Force, Specialized Units Ministry of Interior, Community Development, and Public Security: Burundi National Police (Police Nationale du Burundi, PNB) (2024) Expenditure: 3.5% of GDP (2024 est.)
origin: 1 July 1962 (from UN trusteeship under Belgian administration)
asOf: Archived Factbook edition; individual figures retain their stated years.
